title: Optiling adminlet mesh and runbook compiler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call runs and first-line support increasingly rely on a growing catalog of small admin utilities (adminlets). Each adminlet is hand-wired to a runbook; engineers spend time stitching these into reliable, observable flows. This leads to duplicated safety checks, inconsistent telemetry, and brittle handoffs across support teams.

Goal: Build an "optiling" compiler that turns authored runbooks and adminlet fragments into an executable, typed task mesh. The compiler performs three optimizations: (1) tiling small adminlets into grouped execution units for better batching and permission amortization; (2) automatically injecting standardized safety gates and retry policies; (3) attaching structured telemetry hooks and cost/latency annotations for the Console to surface per-step economics.

Scope: PoC will cover SRE/Support-critical adminlets used for disk reclaim, index rebuild, and emergency model rollback. The deliverable is a compiler binary (+ infra) and a small migration of 6 runbooks to the compiled mesh with dashboards and end-to-end tests.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler can ingest runbook YAML v1 and emit an executable task graph (adminlet mesh) that the operator runtime runs without per-run manual wiring
All compiled adminlet executions emit structured telemetry (trace, step_id, tokens_estimate, wall_time_ms)
Safety gates injected (RBAC check, dry-run flag, explicit confirmation step) are enforced and audited
Batching/tiling reduces average per-step overhead by >= 20% for the migrated runbooks (measured in latency and token cost)
Migration docs and a one-click rollback for each migrated runbook exist in Confluence and as a PR template
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: scoped PoC runbooks, confirmed SRE contacts, created feature branch admin-compiler/optiling-poc
2026-03-05 — Prototype compiler front-end: can parse runbook YAML and produce a normalized IR; initial safety-gate insertion implemented
2026-03-08 — Telemetry hooks added: step_id, step_kind, estimated_tokens, observed_latency; added trace context propagation into operator runtime

2026-03-10 — End-to-end smoke: compiled mesh executed in staging for 'disk-reclaim' runbook; observed 27% reduction in per-step overhead, but saw intermittent permission failures on cross-service adminlets
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Li) — Please include a migration plan for teams outside SRE; add a dry-run migration mode for non-critical namespaces
Security (Elena Martinez) — Approve concept but require KMS-backed audit trail and explicit ephemeral credentialing for tiled adminlets
Design (Samira Noor) — Suggest consolidating user confirmations into a single gated surface when safe to reduce cognitive load on on-call
implementation_notes: Compiler will be implemented in Go (existing operator runtime stack) to reuse runtime task execution primitives
Tiling heuristics: group adminlets touching same service endpoints and compatible RBAC scope within a 2s window; heuristics configurable via Console
Safety gates: default injected checks are (1) RBAC verification, (2) dry-run availability, (3) idempotency tokens, (4) explicit manual confirmation for destructive actions
Telemetry contract: events are emitted to tracing + Console ingestion; tokens_estimate derived from prompt length and model profile mapping
open_risks: Permission explosion when tiled adminlets require disjoint service roles — mitigated with ephemeral credentialing but requires infra work (ENG-271444)
Behavioral regressions due to implicit batching semantics; requires extensive test harness and synthetic dryruns
Possible latency spikes if tiled adminlets trigger cross-region calls; needs smart routing policy integration
next_steps: Finish ephemeral credentialing prototype with security (target: 2026-03-18)
Add comprehensive dry-run validator and compare outputs against baseline runbook runs (target: 2026-03-22)
Create migration playbook and schedule canary migrations for two non-critical runbooks in the 2026-W12 cycle
